q: Why does the keyboard near the hand trigger the whole habitual chain from a mere command to start, until the action becomes second nature?
Why does James argue that the bodily manifestations must first be interposed, so that we feel sorry because we weep rather than weeping because we are sorry?
What is Ribot's foreshortening of recollected time, and why would remembering everything leave us as ill off as if we remembered nothing?
What does James mean by volitional effort is effort of attention, and why does what holds attention determine action?
What distinguishes the explosive will rooted in defective inhibition from the obstructed will?
Why do impressions on the two fovea always appear in the same place, and what are the main conditions of single vision?
Why can a kitten not help pursuing a moving ball, and what do tickling and the crawling fly show about the sensation of motion?
Why is thought within each personal consciousness sensibly continuous, without breach, crack, or division, in the stream of thought?
Why is habit the enormous fly-wheel of society, as when the menagerie-tiger crept back to its cage after the railroad accident?
In the lecture-room, why do some thoughts cohere mutually and some not, when there is no giving or bartering between minds?
Why is the question of free-will insoluble on strictly psychologic grounds, even after effort of attention has been given to an idea?
Why does a blow on the head or rapid loss of blood abolish consciousness, proving the dependence of mental action upon neural change?
